memory_candidates.content: When migrating a shell script from `set -uo pipefail` to `set -euo pipefail`, a `VAR=$(cmd); status=$?` pair immediately after is an -e-hostile pattern: under -e, a failing bare assignment aborts the script on that line, before the status capture or any custom error handling can run. Fix with `VAR=$(cmd) || status=$?` -- the assignment is not the last command in the `||` list, so it is -e-exempt, and `$?` inside the `||` branch still holds the real failing exit code.

A shared shell library meant to be sourced (not executed) must set zero shell options on its own -- sourcing must never change the calling shell's error-handling behavior. Verify this with a suite asserting `$-`/`set -o` output is byte-identical before and after sourcing the library, exercised directly against callers that themselves set no options (e.g. a hook or command-dispatch script sourced mid-shell).
